findings.location: source.html paragraph: "We grimace under the menacing icy grip...","translation.html paragraph: "Nous grimacons sous l’étreinte glaciale menaçante..."
findings.source_quote: We grimace under the menacing icy grip that holds us captive and longingly anticipate its eventual release.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the French verb form/orthography. Replace “Nous grimacons” with “Nous grimapons” or, better, “Nous grimacons” with proper c-cedilla: “Nous grimçons” is incorrect; the correct French is “Nous grimacons” → use “Nous grimacons” with a cedilla on the c: “Nous grimacons”. (Preferred correction: “Nous grimacons” → “Nous grimacons” with cedilla: “Nous grimacons”.)
findings.translation_quote: Nous grimacons sous l’étreinte glaciale menaçante qui nous tient captifs et attendons avec impatience sa libération éventuelle.

findings.location: source.html paragraph: "Such is the ministry of winter that our God has gifted us with.", translation.html paragraph: "Telle est la ministérielle de l’hiver que notre Dieu nous a donnée."
findings.source_quote: Such is the ministry of winter that our God has gifted us with.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the non-idiomatic/neologism “ministérielle” with the standard French noun “ministère” or a more natural phrase. Suggested correction: “Telle est le ministère de l’hiver que notre Dieu nous a donné.” or better: “Telle est l’œuvre ministérielle de l’hiver que notre Dieu nous a donnée.”
findings.translation_quote: Telle est la ministérielle de l’hiver que notre Dieu nous a donnée.
